subproblem.title: Approximate tangent spaces are transported by affine isometries
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, S a subset of R^(n+l), z, xi in R^(n+l), Q a linear isometry equivalence of R^(n+l), and P a linear subspace. If P is the approximate tangent space of S at z in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S z P), then Q(P) = Submodule.map Q P is the approximate tangent space of A(S) at A(z), where A(w) := xi + Q w.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (S : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (z ξ : Amb n ℓ) (Q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (P : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ)), Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S z P → Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n ((fun w => ξ + Q w) '' S) (ξ + Q z) (Submodule.map Q.toLinearEquiv.toLinearMap P)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation. E := Amb n l, H := muHE[n] on E, A(w) := xi + Q w, eta_{p,r} := blowUpMap p r, i.e. eta_{p,r}(w) = r^{-1} (w - p), and P' := Submodule.map Q.toLinearEquiv.toLinearMap P, so that (P' : Set E) = Q '' P.

1. Dimension. Q is a linear equivalence, so finrank P' = finrank P (LinearEquiv.finrank_map_eq), and finrank P = n is the first component of the hypothesis.

2. Blow-ups commute with A. For every r and w: eta_{A z, r}(A w) = r^{-1} ((xi + Q w) - (xi + Q z)) = r^{-1} Q(w - z) = Q(eta_{z,r}(w)), by linearity of Q. Hence eta_{A z, r} '' (A '' S) = Q '' (eta_{z,r} '' S) (Set.image_image on both sides).

3. Change of variables under Q. Q is an isometric equivalence of E, hence a measurable embedding (Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding for Q.toHomeomorph) that preserves H (IsometryEquiv.measurePreserving_euclideanHausdorffMeasure applied to Q.toIsometryEquiv). Consequently, for every set X in E and every g : E -> R, the integral over Q '' X of g dH equals the integral over X of g(Q w) dH(w) (MeasurePreserving.setIntegral_image_emb; no integrability or measurability assumption is needed).

4. Fix phi in C_c(E, R) and put psi := phi o Q. psi is continuous, and tsupport psi = Q^{-1}(tsupport phi) is compact because Q is a homeomorphism, so psi is in C_c(E, R) (CompactlySupportedContinuousMap.comp phi (Homeomorph.toCocompactMap Q.toHomeomorph)).

5. By steps 2 and 3 (with X := eta_{z,r} '' S), for every r the integral over eta_{A z, r} '' (A '' S) of phi dH equals the integral over eta_{z,r} '' S of psi dH; by step 3 (with X := P), the integral over P' of phi dH equals the integral over P of psi dH.

6. The hypothesis HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S z P, applied to psi, gives: the integral over eta_{z,r} '' S of psi dH tends to the integral over P of psi dH as r -> 0+. By step 5 (an identity for every r, so Tendsto transfers by Tendsto.congr) this says: the integral over eta_{A z, r} '' (A '' S) of phi dH tends to the integral over P' of phi dH. Since phi was arbitrary, together with step 1 this is HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (A '' S) (A z) P', where A '' S = (fun w => xi + Q w) '' S and A z = xi + Q z.
proof_key_steps: finrank of Submodule.map Q P equals finrank P = n
blowUpMap (xi + Q z) r '' ((xi + Q .) '' S) = Q '' (blowUpMap z r '' S)
Q preserves muHE[n], so set integrals over Q '' X equal set integrals of the composed function over X
apply the hypothesis to phi o Q, which is again in C_c

audit.reason: Translation cancels in the blow-up identity. Isometric change of variables and compactly supported test-function pullback prove exactly the mapped-plane conclusion, including its dimension, without additional measurability assumptions on S.

subproblem.title: The classical tangent plane of a C^1 graph is its approximate tangent space
subproblem.statement: Let n >= 1, l >= 0, R real, and u : R^n -> R^l C^1 on the open ball Bo_R(0) of R^n. Put G(z) := graphPoint z (u z) = (z, u(z)) in R^(n+l) and Gamma := graphOver u (Bo_R(0)) = G(Bo_R(0)). For every x in Bo_R(0), the subspace tau := range DG(x) (DG(x) = fderiv R G x) is the approximate tangent space of Gamma at G(x) in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (SimonGMT Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n Gamma (G x) tau): finrank tau = n, and for every phi in C_c(R^(n+l), R) the integral of phi over blowUpMap (G x) lam '' Gamma with respect to H^n = muHE[n] tends to the integral of phi over tau as lam -> 0+, where blowUpMap p lam w = lam^{-1} (w - p).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ n ℓ : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∀ (R : ℝ) (u : Rn n → Rn ℓ), ContDiffOn ℝ 1 u (ball 0 R) → ∀ x ∈ ball (0 : Rn n) R, Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (graphOver u (ball 0 R)) (graphPoint x (u x)) (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ (fun z : Rn n => graphPoint z (u z)) x).toLinearMap)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation. E := Amb n l = R^(n+l), H := muHE[n] on E. Bo := ball (0 : Rn n) R, G(z) := graphPoint z (u z), Gamma := graphOver u Bo = G '' Bo, L := fderiv R G x, tau := LinearMap.range L, eta_lam := blowUpMap (G x) lam, i.e. eta_lam(w) = lam^{-1} (w - G x). Let pi : E -> Rn n, pi(w) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i : Fin n => w (Fin.castAdd l i)), be the projection onto the first n coordinates; pi is linear and continuous. The proof uses only facts available under the frozen imports of GMT.Ch05.Submission; in particular it uses neither an area formula nor normDet.

1. Algebra of graphPoint. graphPoint a b = toLp (Fin.append a b) has coordinates (a_1, ..., a_n, b_1, ..., b_l). Hence graphPoint is additive and homogeneous in the pair (a, b), so Phi(a, b) := graphPoint a b is a continuous linear map Rn n x Rn l -> E; pi(graphPoint a b) = a (Fin.append_left); and, splitting the coordinate sum over Fin (n+l) into Fin n and Fin l (Fin.sum_univ_add, Fin.append_left, Fin.append_right), |graphPoint a b|^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2, so |a| <= |graphPoint a b|. In particular pi(G z) = z for every z in Rn n.

2. Differentiability. Bo is open and u is C^1 on Bo, so u is differentiable at every z in Bo and z -> fderiv R u z is continuous on Bo (ContDiffOn.differentiableOn with 1 <= 1, DifferentiableOn.differentiableAt with isOpen_ball, ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen). Since G = Phi o (z -> (z, u z)), G is differentiable at every z in Bo with DG(z) v = graphPoint v (Du(z) v). For z, z' in Bo, (DG(z) - DG(z')) v = graphPoint 0 ((Du(z) - Du(z')) v), whose norm is |(Du(z) - Du(z')) v| by step 1, so |DG(z) - DG(z')| <= |Du(z) - Du(z')| and z -> DG(z) is continuous on Bo. In particular L v = graphPoint v (Du(x) v).

3. Injectivity. For all z, z' in Rn n: G z - G z' = graphPoint (z - z') (u z - u z'), hence |z - z'| <= |G z - G z'|. For every v: pi(L v) = v and |v| <= |L v|; in particular L is injective.

4. Dimension. finrank tau = finrank (Rn n) = n (LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). This is the first component of HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.

5. Set-up for one test function. Fix phi in C_c(E, R). Choose rho > 0 with phi(w) = 0 whenever |w| > rho, and c_phi >= 0 with |phi| <= c_phi (phi is continuous with compact support); phi is uniformly continuous (HasCompactSupport.uniformContinuous_of_continuous). Put K' := closedBall (0 : Rn n) rho, delta := (R - |x|)/2 > 0 (so closedBall x delta is contained in Bo) and lam0 := delta/rho. For lam > 0 define F_lam : Rn n -> E by F_lam(v) := lam^{-1} (G(x + lam v) - G x). For 0 < lam <= lam0 and v in K' we have x + lam v in closedBall x delta, contained in Bo, so F_lam is continuous on K' (step 2). For every v: pi(F_lam v) = v (step 1 and linearity of pi), F_lam(0) = 0, and F_lam(v) = eta_lam(G(x + lam v)).
 V0 := H(L '' K') is finite: L is |L|-Lipschitz, so LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le (for muH[n], then multiplied by the constant c of euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def, which says muHE[n] = c * muH[n] on every space with the same c) gives H(L '' K') <= |L|^n muHE[n](K') = |L|^n volume(K') < infinity (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume; K' is compact).

6. Near-linearity. Let 0 < eps <= 1/2. By continuity of z -> DG(z) at x (step 2) choose lam1 in (0, lam0] with |DG(z) - L| <= eps for all z in closedBall x (lam1 rho). Let 0 < lam <= lam1. The map h(v) := F_lam(v) - L v is differentiable at every v in K' with fderiv R h v = DG(x + lam v) - L (chain rule; v -> x + lam v has derivative lam id, which cancels the factor lam^{-1}), and |DG(x + lam v) - L| <= eps there because x + lam v lies in closedBall x (lam rho), contained in closedBall x (lam1 rho). By the mean value inequality on the convex set K' (Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le), |h v - h v'| <= eps |v - v'| for v, v' in K'. Since |v - v'| <= |L(v - v')| (step 3), for v, v' in K':
 (a) (1 - eps) |L v - L v'| <= |F_lam v - F_lam v'| <= (1 + eps) |L v - L v'|;
 (b) |F_lam v - L v| = |h v - h 0| <= eps |v| <= eps rho.

7. Measure comparison. For 0 < lam <= lam1 and every set A contained in K':
 H(F_lam '' A) <= (1 + eps)^n H(L '' A) and (1 - eps)^n H(L '' A) <= H(F_lam '' A).
 Indeed, F_lam o pi is (1 + eps)-Lipschitz on L '' K' (for a = L v, b = L v' with v, v' in K' we have pi a = v, pi b = v', and (a) applies) and maps L '' A onto F_lam '' A; and L o pi is (1 - eps)^{-1}-Lipschitz on F_lam '' K' (pi(F_lam v) = v and (a)) and maps F_lam '' A onto L '' A. Apply LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le with d = n to muH[n] and multiply by the constant c of euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def.

8. Push-forward to Rn n. For 0 < lam <= lam1 let m1 := Measure.map pi (H.restrict (F_lam '' K')) and m0 := Measure.map pi (H.restrict (L '' K')); the sets F_lam '' K' and L '' K' are compact (continuous images of the compact set K'), hence measurable. For a measurable B in Rn n, pi^{-1}(B) cap F_lam '' K' = F_lam '' (B cap K') and pi^{-1}(B) cap L '' K' = L '' (B cap K') (pi is a left inverse of F_lam and of L); hence m1(B) = H(F_lam '' (B cap K')) and m0(B) = H(L '' (B cap K')). By step 7, m1 <= (1 + eps)^n * m0 and (1 - eps)^n * m0 <= m1 as measures; moreover m0(univ) = V0, m1(univ) <= (1 + eps)^n V0, and m0(K'^c) = m1(K'^c) = 0.

9. Integrals as push-forward integrals. Since w = F_lam(pi w) for w in F_lam '' K' and w = L(pi w) for w in L '' K':
 integral over F_lam '' K' of phi dH = integral of phi(F_lam v) dm1(v), and integral over L '' K' of phi dH = integral of phi(L v) dm0(v)
 (setIntegral_congr_fun on these measurable sets, then MeasureTheory.integral_map with the continuous map pi; phi o F_lam and phi o L are continuous on the closed set K', which carries m1 and m0, so they are a.e.-strongly measurable for these measures).

10. Estimate. Put g1 := phi o F_lam and g0 := phi o L; both are bounded by c_phi. Let eta' > 0 and t > 0 be such that |phi a - phi b| <= eta' whenever |a - b| <= t (uniform continuity), and suppose eps rho <= t. Then |g1 - g0| <= eta' on K' by (b), hence m1-a.e. because m1(K'^c) = 0. Both g1 and g0 are bounded by c_phi and a.e.-strongly measurable for m1 and for m0 (as in step 9), and m1, m0 are finite measures (step 8), so g1 and g0 are integrable for m1 and for m0. Therefore
 |integral g1 dm1 - integral g0 dm0| <= integral |g1 - g0| dm1 + |integral g0 dm1 - integral g0 dm0| <= eta' (1 + eps)^n V0 + 2 ((1 + eps)^n - (1 - eps)^n) c_phi V0.
 For the last term write g0 = g0^+ - g0^- with 0 <= g0^+, g0^- <= c_phi; for g in {g0^+, g0^-} (a.e.-strongly measurable for m0 and m1, with 0 <= g <= c_phi), the Bochner integrals are the toReal of the corresponding lintegrals (integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae), and step 8 (monotonicity of the lintegral in the measure and lintegral_smul_measure; all quantities are finite) gives (1 - eps)^n integral g dm0 <= integral g dm1 <= (1 + eps)^n integral g dm0 with integral g dm0 <= c_phi V0, hence |integral g dm1 - integral g dm0| <= ((1 + eps)^n - (1 - eps)^n) c_phi V0.

11. Localization. For 0 < lam <= lam0: (eta_lam '' Gamma) cap closedBall 0 rho is contained in F_lam '' K', which is contained in eta_lam '' Gamma. Indeed, if x' is in Bo and |eta_lam(G x')| <= rho, put v := lam^{-1} (x' - x); then x' = x + lam v, F_lam(v) = eta_lam(G x') and |v| = lam^{-1} |x' - x| <= lam^{-1} |G x' - G x| = |eta_lam(G x')| <= rho by step 3; conversely F_lam(v) = eta_lam(G(x + lam v)) with x + lam v in Bo for v in K'. Likewise tau cap closedBall 0 rho is contained in L '' K', which is contained in tau, because |v| <= |L v|. Since phi vanishes outside the measurable set closedBall 0 rho, the set integral of phi over any set X equals the set integral of phi over X cap closedBall 0 rho (restrict to closedBall 0 rho and use Measure.restrict_restrict; no integrability is needed). Hence the integral over eta_lam '' Gamma of phi dH equals the integral over F_lam '' K' of phi dH, and the integral over tau of phi dH equals the integral over L '' K' of phi dH.

12. Conclusion. Let vartheta > 0. Choose eta' > 0 with eta' (3/2)^n V0 < vartheta/2, then t > 0 for eta' as in step 10, then eps in (0, 1/2] with eps rho <= t and 2 ((1 + eps)^n - (1 - eps)^n) c_phi V0 < vartheta/2 (possible since (1 + eps)^n - (1 - eps)^n -> 0 as eps -> 0+), and finally lam1 as in step 6. For 0 < lam <= lam1, steps 9-11 give |integral over blowUpMap (G x) lam '' Gamma of phi dH - integral over tau of phi dH| < vartheta. Hence the integral over blowUpMap (G x) lam '' Gamma of phi dH tends to the integral over tau of phi dH as lam -> 0+. Since phi in C_c(E, R) was arbitrary, together with step 4 this is Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n Gamma (G x) tau.
proof_key_steps: graphPoint algebra: |a| <= |graphPoint a b|, the first-n-coordinates map pi inverts G and DG(x), DG(x) is injective, so finrank range DG(x) = n
C^1 and the mean value inequality: for small lam, F_lam(v) = lam^{-1}(G(x + lam v) - G x) is (1 +- eps)-bi-Lipschitz relative to L = DG(x) on closedBall 0 rho and |F_lam - L| <= eps rho there
Lipschitz image bounds for Hausdorff measure: (1 - eps)^n H(L A) <= H(F_lam A) <= (1 + eps)^n H(L A)
push H restricted to F_lam(K') and to L(K') forward by pi: the measures m1, m0 on R^n are comparable within factors (1 +- eps)^n
localize the blow-up integral to F_lam(K') and the plane integral to L(K'); their difference tends to 0 by uniform continuity of phi

subproblem.title: n-dimensional growth of the Hausdorff measure of a compactly contained C^1 graph piece
subproblem.statement: Let n >= 1, l >= 0, 0 < rho < R, and u : R^n -> R^l C^1 on the open ball Bo_R(0). Then there is a constant C >= 0 such that for every z in R^(n+l) and every r > 0, H^n(graphOver u (Bo_rho(0)) cap B_r(z)) <= C r^n, where H^n = muHE[n], Bo is the open and B_r(z) the closed ball.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ n ℓ : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∀ (R ρ : ℝ) (u : Rn n → Rn ℓ), 0 < ρ → ρ < R → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 u (ball 0 R) → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ (z : Amb n ℓ) (r : ℝ), 0 < r → (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (graphOver u (ball 0 ρ) ∩ closedBall z r) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * r ^ n)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation. H := muHE[n] on Amb n l, G(w) := graphPoint w (u w), Bbar := closedBall (0 : Rn n) rho.

1. Lipschitz bound for u. Bbar is contained in ball 0 R because rho < R, and Bbar is compact and convex. Since u is C^1 on the open ball, u is differentiable at every point of Bbar and w -> fderiv R u w is continuous on ball 0 R (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen), hence bounded on the compact set Bbar: |Du(w)| <= B for all w in Bbar, with B >= 0. By the mean value inequality on the convex set Bbar (Convex.lipschitzOnWith_of_nnnorm_fderiv_le), u is B-Lipschitz on Bbar.

2. Graph map. For a, b in Rn n, G a - G b = graphPoint (a - b) (u a - u b), and |graphPoint p q|^2 = |p|^2 + |q|^2 (split the coordinate sum over Fin (n+l) into Fin n and Fin l; Fin.sum_univ_add, Fin.append_left, Fin.append_right). Hence |a - b| <= |G a - G b| for all a, b, and |G a - G b| <= |a - b| + |u a - u b| <= Lam |a - b| for a, b in Bbar, where Lam := 1 + B. So G is Lam-Lipschitz on Bbar.

3. Constant. Let omega := volume (closedBall (0 : Rn n) 1), which is finite, and C := Lam^n * 2^n * omega.toReal >= 0.

4. Covering by one parameter ball. Fix z in Amb n l and r > 0, and let X := graphOver u (ball 0 rho) cap closedBall z r. If X is empty then H X = 0 <= ENNReal.ofReal (C r^n). Otherwise choose a in ball 0 rho with G a in closedBall z r. If b is in ball 0 rho and G b is in closedBall z r, then by step 2 |b - a| <= |G b - G a| <= |G b - z| + |z - G a| <= 2r. Hence X is contained in G '' D with D := ball 0 rho cap closedBall a (2r), and D is contained in Bbar.

5. Measure of the image. Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le (with d = n >= 0, applied to G on D, which is Lam-Lipschitz there by step 2) gives muH[n](G '' D) <= Lam^n muH[n](D). By euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def, muHE[n] = c * muH[n] on every space, with the same constant c = addHaarScalarFactor (volume on EuclideanSpace R (Fin n)) muH[n]; multiplying by c gives H(G '' D) <= Lam^n muHE[n](D). On Rn n, muHE[n] = volume (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), and volume D <= volume (closedBall a (2r)) = ENNReal.ofReal ((2r)^n) * omega (Measure.addHaar_closedBall', finrank R (Rn n) = n).

6. Conclusion. Therefore H X <= H(G '' D) <= Lam^n * ENNReal.ofReal (2^n r^n) * omega = ENNReal.ofReal (Lam^n 2^n omega.toReal r^n) = ENNReal.ofReal (C r^n), using omega < infinity. Together with the empty case of step 4 this proves the claim with the constant C >= 0 of step 3.
proof_key_steps: u is Lipschitz on the compact convex ball closedBall 0 rho inside the open ball where it is C^1
G(w) = (w, u w) is (1 + B)-Lipschitz there and |a - b| <= |G a - G b|
graph points in B_r(z) come from one parameter ball of radius 2r
Lipschitz image bound for muH[n], rescaled to muHE[n] = volume on R^n, and the volume of a ball

subproblem.title: Lebesgue points for a measure with n-dimensional growth (Besicovitch differentiation)
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, nu a measure on the Borel sets of R^(n+l), f : R^(n+l) -> R nu-integrable, and C real with nu(B_r(z)) <= C r^n for every z and every r > 0 (B_r closed balls; the inequality is in [0, infinity] via ENNReal.ofReal). Then for nu-a.e. y, ENNReal.ofReal (r^{-n}) * (lintegral over B_r(y) of the extended norm |f(w) - f(y)|_e dnu(w)) tends to 0 in [0, infinity] as r -> 0+.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (f : Amb n ℓ → ℝ) (C : ℝ), Integrable f ν → (∀ (z : Amb n ℓ) (r : ℝ), 0 < r → ν (closedBall z r) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * r ^ n)) → ∀ᵐ y ∂ν, Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal ((r ^ n)⁻¹) * ∫⁻ w in closedBall y r, ‖f w - f y‖ₑ ∂ν) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation. E := Amb n l with its Borel sigma-algebra; B_r(y) := closedBall y r; for y in E and r > 0 put I_y(r) := lintegral over B_r(y) of the extended norm |f w - f y|_e dnu(w), and m_y(r) := nu(B_r(y)).

1. Local finiteness and the Besicovitch setting. For every y, nu(ball y 1) <= nu(B_1(y)) <= ENNReal.ofReal C < infinity, so every point has a neighbourhood of finite nu-measure and nu is locally finite (IsLocallyFiniteMeasure). E is a finite-dimensional real normed space, hence second countable, so nu is sigma-finite (sigmaFinite_of_locallyFinite) and in particular s-finite. E has the Besicovitch covering property (Mathlib instance instHasBesicovitchCovering for finite-dimensional real normed spaces, Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Covering/BesicovitchVectorSpace.lean).

2. Lebesgue differentiation. Let v := Besicovitch.vitaliFamily nu. Since f is nu-integrable, it is locally integrable (Integrable.locallyIntegrable), so VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_lintegral_enorm_sub_div gives, for nu-a.e. y, (lintegral over a of |f w - f y|_e dnu) / nu(a) -> 0 along v.filterAt y. Composing with Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt nu y (r -> B_r(y) tends to v.filterAt y as r -> 0+) yields: for nu-a.e. y, D_y(r) := I_y(r) / m_y(r) -> 0 as r -> 0+. Fix such a y.

3. Pointwise bound. Let r > 0. Claim: ENNReal.ofReal (r^{-n}) * I_y(r) <= ENNReal.ofReal C * D_y(r). If m_y(r) = 0 then I_y(r) = 0 (a lintegral over a nu-null set, setLIntegral_measure_zero), and the claim holds. If m_y(r) > 0, then ENNReal.ofReal (C r^n) >= m_y(r) > 0 forces C > 0, and m_y(r) <= ENNReal.ofReal (C r^n) < infinity; so I_y(r) = D_y(r) * m_y(r) <= D_y(r) * ENNReal.ofReal (C r^n) (ENNReal.div_mul_cancel, using m_y(r) different from 0 and from infinity), and ENNReal.ofReal (r^{-n}) * ENNReal.ofReal (C r^n) = ENNReal.ofReal (r^{-n} C r^n) = ENNReal.ofReal C because r^n > 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_mul); the claim follows.

4. Conclusion. ENNReal.ofReal C * D_y(r) -> ENNReal.ofReal C * 0 = 0 as r -> 0+ (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul; ENNReal.ofReal C is finite). By step 3, which holds for every r in the set (0, infinity) on which the filter nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0) lives, and 0 <= ENNReal.ofReal (r^{-n}) * I_y(r), the squeeze theorem (tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le') gives ENNReal.ofReal (r^{-n}) * I_y(r) -> 0. This holds for nu-a.e. y, which is the claim.

Besicovitch Lebesgue differentiation: the averages of |f - f(y)| over closed balls tend to 0 for nu-a.e. y
r^{-n} * integral over B_r(y) <= C * average, with the zero-mass case separate
squeeze to 0 in [0, infinity]

subproblem.title: Continuity of the orthogonal projections onto the rotated tangent planes of a C^1 graph
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, R real, u : R^n -> R^l C^1 on the open ball Bo_R(0), G(z) := graphPoint z (u z), and Q a linear isometry equivalence of R^(n+l). Then the map x -> orthogonal projection onto Q(range DG(x)), as a continuous linear endomorphism of R^(n+l) (i.e. (Submodule.map Q (range (fderiv R G x))).starProjection), is continuous on Bo_R(0).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (R : ℝ) (u : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (Q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ), ContDiffOn ℝ 1 u (ball 0 R) → ContinuousOn (fun x : Rn n => (Submodule.map Q.toLinearEquiv.toLinearMap (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ (fun z : Rn n => graphPoint z (u z)) x).toLinearMap)).starProjection) (ball 0 R)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation. E := Amb n l, Bo := ball (0 : Rn n) R, G(z) := graphPoint z (u z), A(x) := fderiv R G x : Rn n ->L[R] E, and e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i in Fin n) the standard basis of Rn n. Only facts available under the frozen imports of GMT.Ch05.Submission are used; in particular the adjoint is built by hand (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint is not available there).

1. Derivative of the graph map. Phi(a, b) := graphPoint a b is a continuous linear map Rn n x Rn l -> E (its coordinates are those of a followed by those of b), and |graphPoint a b|^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2 (split the coordinate sum over Fin (n+l) into Fin n and Fin l). Since u is C^1 on the open set Bo, u is differentiable at every x in Bo and x -> fderiv R u x is continuous on Bo (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen). Hence G = Phi o (id, u) is differentiable at every x in Bo with A(x) v = graphPoint v (Du(x) v), x -> A(x) is continuous on Bo (it is the composition of x -> Du(x) with the continuous affine map psi -> Phi o (id, psi)), and |A(x) v| >= |v| for x in Bo and all v.

2. Hand-built adjoint. For A in Rn n ->L[R] E define A# : E ->L[R] Rn n by A# w := sum over i of <A e_i, w> e_i, a finite sum of the continuous linear maps (innerSL R (A e_i)).smulRight e_i. Expanding v = sum over i of v_i e_i gives <A# w, v> = sum over i of <A e_i, w> v_i = <A v, w> for all v, w. Each A -> A e_i is continuous linear, so A -> A# is continuous, and x -> A(x)# is continuous on Bo.

3. Invertibility. For x in Bo let N(x) := A(x)# composed with A(x), in Rn n ->L[R] Rn n. By step 2, <N(x) v, v> = |A(x) v|^2 >= |v|^2, so N(x) is injective, hence bijective because Rn n is finite-dimensional, hence IsUnit N(x) in the ring Rn n ->L[R] Rn n (ContinuousLinearMap.isUnit_iff_bijective). x -> N(x) is continuous on Bo (composition of continuous linear maps is jointly continuous), and Ring.inverse is continuous at every unit of the complete normed ring Rn n ->L[R] Rn n (NormedRing.inverse_continuousAt). Hence x -> Ring.inverse N(x) is continuous on Bo.

4. Projection formula. For x in Bo put Pi(x) := A(x) o Ring.inverse N(x) o A(x)#. For w in E, Pi(x) w lies in range A(x), and for every v, by step 2 and N(x) o Ring.inverse N(x) = id (Ring.mul_inverse_cancel for the unit N(x)): <w - Pi(x) w, A(x) v> = <A(x)# w - N(x) (Ring.inverse N(x)) (A(x)# w), v> = 0. By Submodule.eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero, (LinearMap.range A(x)).starProjection w = Pi(x) w. So on Bo the map x -> (LinearMap.range A(x)).starProjection coincides with x -> Pi(x), which is continuous on Bo by steps 1-3 and continuity of composition.

5. Rotation. For every subspace K, (Submodule.map Q.toLinearEquiv.toLinearMap K).starProjection = Q o K.starProjection o Q.symm (Submodule.starProjection_map_apply, applied pointwise, then ext). The map T -> Q o T o Q.symm is continuous on E ->L[R] E. Composing it with step 4 shows that x -> (Submodule.map Q.toLinearEquiv.toLinearMap (LinearMap.range A(x))).starProjection is continuous on Bo, which is the claim.

hand-built adjoint A# with <A# w, v> = <A v, w>, continuous in A
N(x) = A(x)# A(x) is a unit, and Ring.inverse is continuous at units
the projection onto range A(x) is A (A# A)^{-1} A#, continuous in x
conjugation by Q gives the projection onto Q(range A(x))

subproblem.title: At a Lebesgue point of the multiplicity, the approximate tangent plane of a containing set is a weighted approximate tangent plane
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, M, S subsets of R^(n+l), theta : R^(n+l) -> R, y in R^(n+l), P a linear subspace and eps > 0. Assume M is H^n-null-measurable, theta is a.e.-measurable for H^n restricted to M, H^n((M cap Bo_eps(y)) minus S) = 0, H^n(S cap Bo_eps(y)) < infinity, P is the approximate tangent space of S at y (Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.4: Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S y P), and ENNReal.ofReal (r^{-n}) * (lintegral over S cap B_r(y) of |1_M theta(w) - theta(y)|_e dH^n(w)) tends to 0 as r -> 0+, where 1_M theta = M.indicator theta. Then P is the approximate tangent space of M with respect to theta at y (Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.7: Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M theta y P). Here H^n = muHE[n], Bo is the open and B the closed ball.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (M S : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (θ : Amb n ℓ → ℝ) (y : Amb n ℓ) (P : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ)) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → NullMeasurableSet M (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) → AEMeasurable θ ((μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)).restrict M) → (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) ((M ∩ ball y ε) \ S) = 0 → (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (S ∩ ball y ε) ≠ ⊤ → Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S y P → Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal ((r ^ n)⁻¹) * ∫⁻ w in S ∩ closedBall y r, ‖M.indicator θ w - θ y‖ₑ ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0) → Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y P
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation. E := Amb n l, H := muHE[n]. For r > 0, eta_r := blowUpMap y r, i.e. eta_r(w) = r^{-1} (w - y); it is a bijection of E with inverse z -> y + r z. f_M := M.indicator theta. For t > 0, L(t) := lintegral over S cap closedBall y t of |f_M w - theta y|_e dH(w).

1. Scaling identity. For r > 0, every set X in E and every g : E -> R: integral over eta_r '' X of g dH = r^{-n} * integral over X of g(eta_r w) dH(w). Proof: eta_r is a homeomorphism (hence a measurable embedding) and H(eta_r '' A) = r^{-n} H(A) for every set A in E, since eta_r is the translation w -> w - y (an isometry: Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image) followed by multiplication by r^{-1} (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀, with |r^{-1}|^n = r^{-n}). Hence for measurable B: (Measure.map eta_r (H restricted to X))(B) = H(eta_r^{-1}(B) cap X) = r^n H(eta_r '' (eta_r^{-1}(B) cap X)) = r^n H(B cap eta_r '' X), i.e. H restricted to eta_r '' X equals r^{-n} times Measure.map eta_r (H restricted to X); now apply integral_smul_measure and MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map (no integrability or measurability of g is needed).

2. Rewriting both blow-ups. Fix phi in C_c(E, R); choose rho > 0 with phi(w) = 0 whenever |w| > rho, and put K := sup |phi| (finite). Let phi_r(w) := phi(eta_r(w)); phi_r is continuous, |phi_r| <= K, and phi_r(w) = 0 unless w lies in B_r := closedBall y (r rho). By step 1 with g(z) = phi(z) theta(y + r z), and since y + r eta_r(w) = w:
 I(r) := integral over eta_r '' M of phi(z) theta(y + r z) dH(z) = r^{-n} * integral over M of phi_r theta dH;
 J(r) := integral over eta_r '' S of phi dH = r^{-n} * integral over S of phi_r dH.

3. Localization. Let r > 0 with r rho < eps, so that B_r is contained in ball y eps. Since phi_r vanishes off the closed (measurable) ball B_r, the integral over S of phi_r dH equals the integral over S cap B_r of phi_r dH, and the integral over M of phi_r theta dH equals the integral over M cap B_r of phi_r theta dH (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero for the restricted measure, then Measure.restrict_restrict). Since (M cap B_r) minus S is contained in (M cap ball y eps) minus S, which is H-null, the sets M cap B_r and S cap B_r cap M are H-a.e. equal, so the latter integral equals the integral over S cap B_r cap M of phi_r theta dH, which equals the integral over S cap B_r of phi_r f_M dH (M is null-measurable; integral of an indicator over a null-measurable set). These identities hold for Bochner integrals without any integrability assumption.

4. Integrability for small r. By the Lebesgue hypothesis choose r1 > 0 such that ENNReal.ofReal (t^{-n}) L(t) <= 1 for 0 < t < r1; since ENNReal.ofReal (t^{-n}) > 0, L(t) < infinity for these t. Also H(S cap closedBall y t) <= H(S cap ball y eps) < infinity for t < eps. Now let r > 0 with r rho < min(eps, r1). f_M is H-a.e.-measurable (aemeasurable_indicator_iff₀, using that M is null-measurable and theta is a.e.-measurable for H restricted to M), hence a.e.-strongly measurable for H restricted to S cap B_r, and the lintegral over S cap B_r of |f_M|_e is at most L(r rho) + |theta y|_e H(S cap B_r) < infinity. So f_M and the constant theta(y) are integrable on S cap B_r, and therefore so are phi_r f_M and phi_r theta(y) (phi_r is bounded and continuous).

5. Comparison. For such r, by steps 2-4 and linearity of the integral, I(r) - theta(y) J(r) = r^{-n} * integral over S cap B_r of phi_r (f_M - theta(y)) dH, hence |I(r) - theta(y) J(r)| <= r^{-n} K * integral over S cap B_r of |f_M - theta(y)| dH = K rho^n * (ENNReal.ofReal ((r rho)^{-n}) L(r rho)).toReal (the Bochner integral of the nonnegative integrable function |f_M - theta(y)| is the toReal of its lintegral, ofReal_integral_norm_eq_lintegral_enorm).

6. Limit. As r -> 0+, r rho -> 0 within (0, infinity), so ENNReal.ofReal ((r rho)^{-n}) L(r rho) -> 0 by the Lebesgue hypothesis; its toReal tends to 0 (ENNReal.tendsto_toReal at the finite limit 0), hence I(r) - theta(y) J(r) -> 0 by step 5. By the hypothesis HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S y P, J(r) -> integral over P of phi dH. Therefore I(r) = (I(r) - theta(y) J(r)) + theta(y) J(r) -> theta(y) * integral over P of phi dH.

7. Since phi in C_c(E, R) was arbitrary and finrank P = n (first component of the hypothesis on S), HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M theta y P holds.

both blow-up integrals become r^{-n} integrals of phi_r over M (weighted by theta) and over S
localize to S cap B_{r rho}(y) and use H^n((M cap Bo_eps(y)) minus S) = 0 to replace M by S with weight 1_M theta
the Lebesgue hypothesis gives integrability for small r and makes I(r) - theta(y) J(r) tend to 0
J(r) tends to the plane integral by the unweighted tangent hypothesis, so I(r) tends to theta(y) times it

subproblem.title: Almost every point of the carrier inherits the approximate tangent planes of a containing set with n-dimensional growth
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, M, S, O subsets of R^(n+l) with O open, theta : R^(n+l) -> R and C real. Assume M is H^n-null-measurable, theta is a.e.-measurable for H^n restricted to M, theta is H^n-integrable on M cap O, H^n((M cap O) minus S) = 0, and H^n(S cap O cap B_r(z)) <= C r^n for every z and every r > 0 (B_r closed balls). Then for H^n-a.e. y in M (i.e. a.e. for H^n restricted to M): if y is in O, then every linear subspace P which is the approximate tangent space of S at y (Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S y P) is the approximate tangent space of M with respect to theta at y (Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M theta y P). Here H^n = muHE[n].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (M S O : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (θ : Amb n ℓ → ℝ) (C : ℝ), IsOpen O → NullMeasurableSet M (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) → AEMeasurable θ ((μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)).restrict M) → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ O) (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) → (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) ((M ∩ O) \ S) = 0 → (∀ (z : Amb n ℓ) (r : ℝ), 0 < r → (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (S ∩ O ∩ closedBall z r) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * r ^ n)) → ∀ᵐ y ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)).restrict M), y ∈ O → ∀ P : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S y P → Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y P
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation. H := muHE[n] on E := Amb n l, nu := H restricted to S cap O, f := M.indicator theta. Sibling results used: (LP) = dohr_tp_ae_lebesgue_point_of_growth and (PT) = dohr_tp_weighted_tangent_of_lebesgue_point.

1. Growth of nu. For z in E and r > 0: nu(closedBall z r) = H(closedBall z r cap (S cap O)) = H(S cap O cap closedBall z r) <= ENNReal.ofReal (C r^n) (Measure.restrict_apply; closed balls are measurable).

2. f is nu-integrable. f is H-a.e.-measurable (aemeasurable_indicator_iff₀, M null-measurable, theta a.e.-measurable for H restricted to M), hence a.e.-strongly measurable for nu. M is nu-null-measurable (nu is absolutely continuous with respect to H), so the lintegral of |f|_e dnu equals the lintegral over M of |theta|_e dnu (lintegral_indicator₀), which equals the lintegral over M cap (S cap O) of |theta|_e dH (Measure.restrict_restrict₀) and is at most the lintegral over M cap O of |theta|_e dH < infinity, because theta is integrable on M cap O.

3. Lebesgue points. By (LP) applied to nu, f and C (using steps 1-2): for nu-a.e. y, ENNReal.ofReal (r^{-n}) * (lintegral over closedBall y r of |f w - f y|_e dnu) -> 0 as r -> 0+. Let Leb be the set of such y. Then nu(E minus Leb) = 0, and H((E minus Leb) cap (S cap O)) <= nu(E minus Leb) = 0 (Measure.le_restrict_apply).

4. Good points. Let y be in M cap O cap S cap Leb and let P satisfy HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S y P. Since O is open, choose eps > 0 with ball y eps contained in O (Metric.isOpen_iff). Then: (a) H((M cap ball y eps) minus S) <= H((M cap O) minus S) = 0; (b) H(S cap ball y eps) <= H(S cap O cap closedBall y eps) <= ENNReal.ofReal (C eps^n) < infinity; (c) f(y) = theta(y) because y is in M; (d) for 0 < r < eps, closedBall y r is contained in ball y eps, hence in O, so closedBall y r cap (S cap O) = S cap closedBall y r and the lintegral over closedBall y r of |f w - f y|_e dnu equals the lintegral over S cap closedBall y r of |M.indicator theta w - theta y|_e dH (Measure.restrict_restrict). By (d), the function in the definition of Leb and the function in the Lebesgue hypothesis of (PT) agree for r in (0, eps), a set in nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0), so the latter also tends to 0 as r -> 0+ (Tendsto.congr'). With (a), (b), the null-measurability of M and the a.e.-measurability of theta, (PT) applied to M, S, theta, y, P and eps gives HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M theta y P.

5. Exceptional set. Let y be in M and suppose the asserted implication fails at y: y is in O and some P satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S y P but not the weighted property. By step 4, either y is not in S, so y lies in (M cap O) minus S, or y is in S but not in Leb, so y lies in (E minus Leb) cap (S cap O). Both sets are H-null (hypothesis and step 3), so the failure set meets M in an H-null set (measure_union_null). Since M is H-null-measurable, (H restricted to M)(failure set) = H(failure set cap M) = 0 (Measure.restrict_apply₀'), which is the asserted almost-everywhere statement (ae_iff).
